title: Prediction sheet
subject: Science
unit: Spring 1: Everyday materials and how they change (Muck, Mess & Mixtures and Will It Degrade?)
source: Seeded from science/y2 lesson 8 (Prediction sheet (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 8: Will it degrade? Setting up a soil test. To understand how to set up a fair test to see which materials degrade in soil

questions.model: Peel is part of a plant. Plants rot in soil. So I predict it will degrade quickly.

questions.q: Predict: will a plastic bag degrade?
questions.a: No, not for a very long time

questions.q: Why do we use the same soil in every jar?
Core: With an adult, set up four jars (peel, paper, plastic, cloth). Label them and write your prediction for each.
questions.a: Peel: rots fast; paper: rots slowly; cotton cloth: rots slowly; plastic: does not rot
questions.model: Teacher shows it first: soil in the jar, peel in the middle, more soil on top, two spoons of water, label 'peel: I think it will rot'.

questions.q: Extend: Why do you think plastic does not rot?
questions.a: It is made by people and microbes cannot break it down easily

questions.q: Stretch: How could this help us look after the earth?
questions.a: Use less plastic and compost food peel

questions.q: Big question: what happens to rubbish when it is buried in soil?
questions.a: Natural things like peel rot away; plastic stays for a very long time
